**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Leave the owner-held naming decision unanswered**

In this pre-decision report, calling this the “single practice ... most worth naming” answers and ranks the exact owner-held question later posed in §7.4 (“Is ... a practice worth naming here?”). That contradicts both the report's stated non-goal and the authority split in `.agent/reports/README.md`, so the exploration should describe the observed mechanism and decision factors without selecting it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**Over-bar** (prong one: a reader takes a steer the contract forbids). Cured in SHA:4114e2447: the sentence now names the practice as distinct and points at §7's fourth question, which stays open. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Narrow the reproducibility claim**

This promise is false for the report's most material numbers: §5.2 says the 33,684/5,737-token results and 82–94% savings came from an unavailable internal Java corpus and are not independently checkable, while reproduction step 5 merely prints the published table and counts different fixtures. A reviewer following the success contract therefore cannot reproduce every number; scope this claim to the metadata, arithmetic, and fixture mismatch that the supplied commands actually verify, or provide the missing corpus and execution evidence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**Over-bar** (prong one: a reader following the success contract fails). Cured in SHA:4114e2447: the promise is scoped to repository-derived numbers (§2, §3, §5.2, §5.3) and names the external inputs — the npm registry metadata, the shell probe, the on-disk size, the README's benchmark corpus. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

The inventory above lists three host manifests plus two marketplace manifests, so there are five manifest JSON files, not four. Since this row is verifying the three host manifests that point at `skills/`, the evidence description should say which set was read rather than claiming an impossible four-manifest total.

**Over-bar** (an evidence row a reader trusts). Cured in SHA:4114e2447: the row reads "the three host manifests and the two marketplace manifests (five files)" and names the Claude Code and Codex manifests as the two the report shows pointing at `skills/` (§3.1 tree). The round-two suppressed assertion that the Cursor manifest does not point at `skills/` is unverified at this seat — the subject repository is out of scope for this settlement — and is not written in. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

This blanket claim contradicts §5.2 immediately above: the published benchmark values are explicitly not reproducible from the committed fixtures/runner, and the npm metadata was fetched externally rather than from the pinned subject. Narrow this sentence so the reproduction guarantee applies only to repository-derived checks.

**Over-bar**, the same finding as the Codex thread at this anchor (matched on anchor and substance; counted once). Cured in SHA:4114e2447 as described there. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Separate executable shunt code from the manifest-only plugin**

This description applies to the whole `portal-ai-plugins` repository, but §3.3 later inventories executable hooks and scripts plus two additional shunt skills, so the repository does ship application code and contains more than the six portal skills. A reader using this opening summary to assess the repository would therefore miss its principal implementation surface; scope the manifest-only claim to the portal plugin and describe shunt separately.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**Over-bar** (prong one: a reader assessing the repository misses its implementation surface). Cured in SHA:4114e2447: §1 scopes "no application code / six skills / one dependency" to the portal plugin and states that shunt ships hooks, transport scripts, two skills and an eval harness with `jq` as a prerequisite — every item already in the report's own §3.3 and §4.2. The index row in `.agent/reports/README.md` is re-trued to match. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Qualify the hard-gate claim around its documented bypass**

When a large read is placed in a compound Bash command containing any pipe or redirect, §5.3 shows that `check-bash-read` immediately allows it, for example `cat big.ts; echo done > /dev/null`. In that scenario the expensive path remains open, so saying the hook catches these commands and leaves only the cheap path contradicts the report's own source-derived finding; narrow this to the direct command forms the matcher actually blocks.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**Over-bar** (prong one). Cured in SHA:4114e2447: the enforcement claim is bounded to the full-file reads the hooks cover, with the gate's edges named by cross-reference — the compound-command bypass (§5.3) and code-writer's absence of enforcement (§3.4). Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark server-side retention as an unverified subject claim**

For readers evaluating privacy, billing, or replay behaviour, “nothing is stored server-side” is presented here as a design fact even though §5.4 explicitly lists the ephemerality of `aika:invoke-chat` among the runtime claims that were not verified. This also misses the report's own contract that subject assertions be marked throughout; attribute the statement directly to the subject README rather than asserting it as established behaviour.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**Over-bar on prong one** — a privacy or billing reader acts on §4.2 alone. Cured in SHA:4114e2447: the prerequisites paragraph is attributed to the README and the server-side claim is marked as one §5.4 lists unverified. Note: the review contract's per-claim marker promise was narrowed in the same push (it overstated the marking discipline the report actually uses; the editing seat is named under the byline); this cure stands on prong one, not on the contract. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep seat interpretation out of the owner-authored entry**

The `author` field makes the entire entry an Owner-authored decision, but only the short quoted sentence is owner-verbatim; the claims that “touch” means never reading or scanning `.env` files and that redaction must use output-shape matching are the seat's derived implementation interpretation. Future readers will treat that extra constraint and remedy as owner authority, so retain only the quoted decision here or explicitly separate and attribute the subsequent reasoning as the recorder's reading.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**Over-bar** (the implementer would read the seat's reading as the owner's ruling — the owner named this exact failure on 2026-09-12). Cured in SHA:4114e2447: entry-004 carries the owner's verbatim sentence and "Option C" alone under `author: Owner`; the recorder's reading (what "touch" forbids; redaction as output-shape matching) moved to entry-005 under the prefix "The recorder's reading (Nettle guards Pistil, 2de368), not the owner's word". Entry ids unchanged. Evidence class RUN — `validate-collaboration-state` green on the push.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cite the decision instead of copying it into the thread**

This closed decision's outcome and constraints are copied into the thread immediately after the record says the body is not restated, and the same material is copied again in the new compaction-boundary section. `.agent/memory/operational/threads/README.md` explicitly makes the conversation file the decision body and requires thread records to cite it, because parallel copies can drift; keep the path and actionable follow-up here without duplicating the decision text.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**Below-bar** under PDR-140 clause 9(a): the copied text is accurate today and no reader is misled by it. The DRY defect is real and the record's own convention (cite the conversation file, never copy it) applies at the record's next write — the successor fold's re-true. Rejected with rationale; no write in the rebudgeted push (clause 9(b)). Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refresh the authoritative handoff during the fold**

This boundary records zero open PRs and new owner priorities, but the reviewed change never refreshes `.agent/memory/operational/director-handoff.md`, even though this record's opening pointer tells a resuming Director that its `CURRENT HANDOFF STATE` is authoritative. In the reviewed tree that snapshot still names the 2026-09-10 coordination branch and the obsolete #108/#110/#109/#100/#103 lanes, so a successor following the documented pickup path receives stale routing instead of the state recorded here; update the live handoff snapshot as part of this fold.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**Over-bar** (prong one: a resuming Director following the documented pickup path is misrouted). Cured in SHA:4114e2447: `director-handoff.md` §CURRENT HANDOFF STATE — the fold block and the live snapshot replaced in place, like for like, per the file's own refresh contract; no 2026-09-10 lane is named; `SHA:` prefixes throughout. Evidence class READ.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve cure-worthy counts in the verdict slice**

If the owner approves this recorded plan, the proposed row carries only `raised`, so the terminal-zero and step-back verdicts can only operate on raw findings (or resolution state). The ratified `.agent/plans/delivery/pr-tally.plan.md` instead defines the predicate over a distinct cure-worthy count derived from the bar marker: for example, a round containing only below-bar findings must be terminal zero even though `raised > 0`. Deferring both cure-worthiness and its marker while implementing the verdict therefore entrenches the wrong state machine; include that field and input in this slice or defer the verdict with them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**Over-bar on prong two** (changes what gets built). Cured in SHA:4114e2447 in two places: the thread record no longer carries the slice — it cites the ratified node as the only home of the design; and `pr-tally.plan.md` carries a `## Review dispositions` row for this finding with its pickup disposition (todo 3, the bar marker, lands first per the node's own sequencing; todo 1's row carries the cure-worthy count). Evidence class READ; `validate-plan-corpus` green.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Sort tally rows by branch commit order**

When a review for an older head arrives after a review for a newer head, first-appearance order is review-arrival order rather than branch commit order. That reverses or interleaves the `c[n]` sequence consumed by the next step's convergence predicate, producing a false step-back or terminal verdict; the ratified plan explicitly requires commit order, never arrival order. Pass an authoritative head-order input to `buildRows` and sort bindings against it instead of preserving first appearance.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**Over-bar on prong two.** Cured in SHA:4114e2447 the same way: the rival slice is removed from the record, and the node's ledger row records the pickup disposition — `buildRows` takes an authoritative head-order input and sorts bindings against it, never first appearance. Evidence class READ; `validate-plan-corpus` green.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

This calls todo 3 an “approved settlement plan” and says the owner's go is answered, but this same record says the owner had not yet answered at lines 2313-2315 and still had not ruled on the slice boundary at lines 2364-2366; the PR description makes the same pending-status claim. That contradiction can cause the next seat to treat todo 3 as owner-approved scope. Please keep this as a standing proposal until the owner decision is recorded, or reconcile all three surfaces with the actual ruling.

— Nettle guards Pistil (2de368), Director

This says the two-hour slice is “written out here in full”, but the following section only points to `pr-tally.plan.md`, records two review dispositions, and gives a short sequencing summary; the promised time-boxed steps and explicit leaves are not present in this thread record. A successor therefore cannot recover the plan from the durable record as claimed. Include the full slice here, or change the wording to identify the actual home of the complete plan.

Cured in `SHA:b50820152`: the sentence now says the slice was written out here at the boundary and is retained by git at `SHA:be6f75c05`, not reproduced; the actual home of the complete design is the ratified node, which this section cites. Evidence class READ.
